service.description: The caller's first personal key, made in their client: both public halves (public, the vault crate's 64 bytes as hex), the private halves wrapped by the key passphrase (passphraseWrap, refused under the Argon2id floor or over its ceiling) and by the recovery code (recoveryWrap). personalKeyId is the client's (it is bound into the wraps). Needs a strong, recent sign-in as get#WrappedPersonalKey does, so a weak session or a key cannot plant a key for a user who has none. Refused when the caller has an active key (replace#PersonalKey). A taken id, or one a deleted record had, is "not available". An event.

The caller's active personal key: its public halves and fingerprint, never a wrap; and whether get#WrappedPersonalKey would send its wraps now (fetchAllowed); the caller's userId, which their client signs as.

The caller's own wrapped personal key (the passphrase wrap and the recovery code's wrap), only after a strong sign-in in the last vault@key-fetch-max-age seconds: a password and a second factor, SSO, or a paired device's key with a recent sign-in on it; never an app password or a login, API or scoped key, never a password alone (plans/Vault-Instances.md §9). Refused otherwise, saying to set up a second factor (reasonCode strongAuthNeedsFactor) or to confirm it is you (strongAuthRequired). An event.
A new key passphrase: the caller's active key's new passphrase wrap (and, when given, a new recovery code's wrap), after a strong, recent sign-in as for get#WrappedPersonalKey. An event.

A new personal key in place of the caller's active one (the passphrase and the recovery code both lost), after a strong, recent sign-in. The old key is marked replaced; nothing is wrapped to the new key until a member, or the recovery key, has checked its fingerprint (add#VaultMember). An event.
Another user's active personal key, by userId or username: its public halves and fingerprint, to compare by another channel before adding them as a member or sending them a delivery.

A key check the caller made after comparing a fingerprint (check, the vault crate's shape), signed by their own active key, of a personal key as it is stored (both halves) or of the lease key. Refused otherwise. A later check of the same key by the same key replaces the earlier.
The caller's own key checks, in the vault crate's shape (with keyCheckId), for their client to verify with its own key and use; optionally those of one checked key.

A vault. vaultId is the client's (it is bound into the wraps). Single-secret (lockEnumId VlSingleSecret): personal only, its vault key wrapped by the password or generated key (secretKindEnumId, secretWrap); a member list or recovery is refused. Shared-key (VlSharedKey): the first key version (entry, 1.1, signed by the caller with their active key as a manager in it) and a wrap of the vault key to every member it lists (memberWraps, signed by a manager), each member's active key checked by the caller (store#KeyCheck). A personal vault's name goes in headerCipher (sealed) and never in vaultName; an operational vault (VkOperational) needs VAULT_ADMIN, has its vaultName, and keeps recovery on or at least two members. Recovery is on when the first member list lists the organization's recovery key (recovery:recoveryKeyId, a manager, its maker's key checked by the caller) with a wrap; recoveryOn Y without it is refused, and a single-secret vault never has it. An event.
The vaults the caller is a member of (their role), and their single-secret vaults: kind, lock, key version, revision, item count, an operational vault's name and a personal vault's sealed header.

To a member (or a single-secret vault's owner): the vault, its member-list chain (entries, oldest first, in the vault crate's shape), its current members and roles, the caller's own wraps of every key version they hold (wraps), a single-secret vault's wrapped key (secretWrap), and an operational vault's deposit key (deposit, the vault crate's shape, whose signature the client checks on each open, and its private half wrapped by the vault key, depositWrappedPrivate). Anyone else is told there is no such vault.

A single-secret vault's owner stores its vault key wrapped again (secretWrap): a password's wrap raised to the Argon2id target on an open (the vault crate's vault_key_password_open answers it as rewrapped), a new password, or a generated key (secretKindEnumId changes the kind). Needs a strong, recent sign-in, as fetching a wrapped personal key does; a password's wrap under the Argon2id floor or over its ceiling is refused. Names the vault revision it was made from (expectedRevision). An event.

A personal vault's header (its name) sealed again by the client under the vault's current key version (the vault crate's header_seal answers it as header_cipher): a rename. A manager of a shared-key vault, or a single-secret vault's owner; an operational vault's name is in the clear and is refused here. Names the vault revision it was made from (expectedRevision). An event.

parameter.name: keyVersion
parameter.description: The key version it is sealed under; refused when it is not the vault's.

service.description: A manager (or a single-secret vault's owner) deletes the vault with its items, their history, its members, key versions and recovery wraps, after a recent sign-in (require#RecentAuth's rule); an operational vault also needs VAULT_ADMIN. Its events stay, and its id is never given to another vault. An event.

An item, by a member who may write (manage or write in a personal vault, manage in an operational one; a single-secret vault's owner): its item key wrapped by the vault key and its sealed body, at the vault's current keyVersion (another version is refused). vaultItemId is the client's. A personal vault's item gives no type, binding or name (they are in its body); an operational item gives all three, the binding unique in its vault. At most 64 KiB. An event.

A new revision of an item, naming the revision it was made from (expectedRevision; a stale one is refused), at the vault's current keyVersion (after a removal, a write at the old version is refused). The revision before is kept in VaultItemHistory. An operational item keeps its type, binding and name unless all three are given, a new binding free in the vault. Every item write moves the vault's revision, so a removal made from an earlier read is refused. An event.

parameter.name: newItemKey
parameter.description: The client made a new item key for this write (the vault crate's item_seal answers new_item_key): an environment's machine access to the item goes stale and is given again

parameter.name: rotated
parameter.description: The value was changed at its source by hand (a credential the manager cannot rotate, plans/Vault-Instances.md §4.7): the item's age starts again (rotatedDate). Taking a deposit in, or changing notes, leaves it

service.description: A vault's items, to a member: each wrapped item key, its key version and revision, and a personal item's sealed body; an operational item's type, binding and name, and no body (a reveal is by role, V2).

An item's earlier revisions, newest first, to a member of its vault; and a rotation's new values staged or kept as pending (pendingList, plans/Vault-Instances.md §4.7). An operational item's bodies are left out: reveal#VaultItem sends one to the reveal role.

A member who may write takes in an item the server deposited (a provision's credential, or a rotation's new revision): its item key, which their client unwrapped with the deposit key's private half and wrapped by the vault key (the vault crate's deposit_adopt), at the vault's current keyVersion, naming the revision it was made from (expectedRevision). The body stays as it is; the revision before is kept in VaultItemHistory. A lease can name the item after this. Refused for an item that is not a deposit. An event.

An operational item's own rotation age in days (1 to 3650), over its type's (VaultItemType.rotationDays), by a manager of its vault; empty clears it. Past its age from rotatedDate the item is due (plans/Vault-Instances.md §4.7). An event.
An item and its history, by a member who may write, after a recent sign-in. An event.

A manager adds a member, or changes one member's role or personal key: the next revision of the member list at the same key version (entry, signed by the caller with their active key) and the wrap of the current vault key to that member (wrap), both accepted by the vault's chain. The member's key is their active one and the caller has a stored check of it: nothing is wrapped to a new or changed key before its fingerprint is checked. Adding the organization's recovery key (recovery:recoveryKeyId, after checking its maker's key) turns recovery on. The change names the vault revision it was made from (expectedRevision). An event.

parameter.name: rewraps
parameter.description: When the change demotes a manager or changes a manager's key: a new wrap, by a manager of the new list, for each member whose wrap of this key version that manager signed; the change is refused without them.

service.description: A manager removes another member (userId) and rotates the vault key, all in one transaction that names the vault revision it was made from (expectedRevision): revision 1 of the next key version without the member (entry), every item key rewrapped under it (itemKeys: item_id, wrapped_item_key), every remaining member's wrap remade (memberWraps). The removed member's wraps are deleted, and a write at the old version is refused from then on; the others' earlier wraps stay until they open the new version (ack#VaultKeyVersion). Removing the recovery key's member turns recovery off; listing a new recovery key in the same rotation replaces it (after a recovery used it). A vault keeps a manager, and an operational vault recovery on or two members. An operational vault takes the new version's deposit key the rotation made (deposit, depositWrappedPrivate, signed by the caller), else its deposit key is cleared. Two events: the removal and the rotation. A removed member may have kept item keys or values, so the answer of an operational vault's removal offers to rotate the credentials at their source (rotationOffer: each item's binding, name, whether the instance manager can rotate it, else what to do by hand; plans/Vault-Instances.md §3.9, §4.7), which request#InstanceRotation does.

parameter.name: itemKeys
parameter.description: Every item's key; none for a vault with no items

parameter.name: headerCipher
parameter.description: A personal vault's header sealed again under the new key version (the vault crate's vault_rotate answers it, given the old one): required when the vault has a header

service.description: The caller opened keyVersion of the vault key: their wraps of earlier versions are deleted. An event.

A manager of an operational vault puts its deposit key, made in their client (the vault crate's deposit_key_new): its public half signed by the caller with their active key, of the vault's current key version (deposit), and its private half wrapped by the vault key (depositWrappedPrivate). The server checks the signature against the vault's signed member list and refuses a deposit key with no manager's signature or of an earlier key version; the change names the vault revision (expectedRevision). The server then deposits a new item it makes (a password while provisioning) by wrapping its item key to the public half, and cannot read it back. An event.

A lease of an operational vault's items (bindings: a list, or one per line or comma) for an operation a person starts by hand, asked by a member of the vault or a holder of VAULT_ADMIN (the framework's own operations ask in Rust). The server makes the lease's key pair, keeps its private half in this cluster member's memory only, and signs the lease with its lease key: its id, the vault and key version, each item's id, type, binding and name, the operation, the cluster member, the time limit (limitMinutes, at most vault@lease-max-hours) and the lease's public key (lease, the vault crate's shape). The vault's approvers are notified (topic VaultLeaseWaiting). An item the server deposited is refused until a member takes it in. An event.

A lease, to a member of its vault, its requester or a holder of VAULT_ADMIN: its state, the signed statement (lease, which the lease dialog shows and the approver's client checks against the lease key its user checked, never a column), the items' wrapped keys the approver unwraps (wrappedItemKeys, by item id), the lease key and its fingerprint, who asked and approved and when, and whether this cluster member holds its key (held).

A vault's leases, newest first, to its members (statusId: VlsRequested waiting, VlsOpen, VlsEnded, VlsRevoked); with no vault, the leases waiting for the caller's approval and those they asked for, or every lease to a holder of VAULT_ADMIN. Never a sealed key.

A member with the approve role in the lease's vault approves it, on any cluster member, after a recent sign-in: the item keys their client unwrapped (each under the type, binding and name the lease gives) and sealed to the lease's key, with their signature over the lease (approval, the vault crate's lease_approve answer). The server checks its own signature on the lease, the approver's signature with their active key, that every item the lease names is sealed once, and that the vault key has not changed; it stores the approval with the VeLeaseApproved event in one transaction and, at its commit, wakes the member that holds the lease. A lease past its time limit, or not waiting, is refused. The SSH admin shell does not approve.

A lease waiting or open, revoked by a manager or an approver of its vault, its requester or a holder of VAULT_ADMIN: its row is marked revoked with its event, and the member that holds it forgets its keys (told by the cluster topic, and refusing any use once it reads the row).

The server's lease key (the Ed25519 public key that signs each lease) and its fingerprint, which a member compares once by another channel and stores as a key check (store#KeyCheck with the lease key).

A holder of VAULT_ADMIN asks to give an environment (environmentId) machine access to named items of an operational vault (bindings). The server makes a lease for the grant, which a member with the approve role approves as any lease; once it opens, the member that asked seals each item key under the machine key (HKDF of entity-facade@crypt-pass until Sealed-Secrets S1) with the environment, vault and item ids as associated data, in a column the entity facade never decrypts, and ends the lease. These items are then as strong as the server's own keys. Events.
A vault's machine access to its members (vaultId), or every environment's to a holder of VAULT_ADMIN: the environment, the item with its binding and name, who gave it and when; never a sealed key.

A holder of VAULT_ADMIN deletes an environment's sealed item keys of a vault (or of one item, vaultItemId), with an event each, and is given the items to rotate at their source (rotateItemIds), since the server could have kept them.

The calling desktop or mobile app remembers the caller's active personal key (personalKeyId, refused when it is not that key) for minutes, at most vault@device-memory-max-hours; the key stays on the device. Only a device's key may ask. Answers when the record ends (thruStamp, epoch millis), which the device takes as its limit, and the record's secret (memorySecret), the server's half of the memory's key.

Whether the caller's device memory is still good (live): before its time and for their active personal key; while it is, its thruStamp and secret (memorySecret), without which the device cannot open the key from memory. Only a device's key may ask. A device forgets the memory when the answer is no.
Ends the caller's device memory record: the device forgot the key, or the user takes the device off the list, after which it does not open the key from memory again.
The caller's devices that remember their personal key now (deviceMemoryId, deviceName, createdDate, thruStamp), for the Vault key settings.

One operational item's wrapped key and sealed body, with its type, binding and name, to a member with the reveal role, whose client opens it with the vault key. The VeReveal event is written first, in the same transaction. Otherwise the server sends no operational body to any client. With pendingId: a rotation's new value of the item kept as pending (list#VaultItemHistory's pendingList), wrapped to the deposit key, to recover it when the rotation could not put the old value back (plans/Vault-Instances.md §4.7).

A delivery the caller sealed to a user's active personal key and signed with their own active key (delivery, the vault crate's shape; its delivery_id is the client's). Refused when the signature is not the caller's, or the key is not the recipient's active one. An event.

The caller's deliveries (not yet filed, unless includeFiled), each with the sender key's public halves, which the client checks against a key its user checked before it opens the value. Only the recipient lists a delivery.
The recipient filed a delivery's value into a vault in their client. Only the recipient. An event.

The organization's recovery key, made in the caller's client (the vault crate's recovery_make): its record (record: id, public halves, k and n, signed by the caller's active key) and one share per holder (shares, each wrapped to the holder's active personal key and signed by the caller), kept by user group (userGroupId) or instance (instanceId). Needs VAULT_RECOVERY and a recent sign-in; each holder holds VAULT_RECOVERY and the caller has a stored check of each other holder's key; 2 ≤ k ≤ n. A taken id is "not available". An event.

The recovery keys that have not ended (optionally of one userGroupId): each its signed record, its maker's public halves (makerPublic, which a client checks against a key its user checked) and its holders with their keys' public halves; to a caller with VAULT_RECOVERY also each holder's sealed share (held).

A holder starts a recovery: the session their client signed (session, the vault crate's recovery_session_start: its id, the recovery key, the vault, the member and their new active personal key, the client's ephemeral public key). The vault lists that recovery key, the member is a person in its member list, the key is new to it, and the caller has a stored check of it. Needs VAULT_RECOVERY and a recent sign-in. An event and a notice to every member of the vault.

To a holder with VAULT_RECOVERY: the open recoveries of the recovery keys they hold, each its signed session, the recovering holder's public halves, the new key's fingerprint, the vault, and who has sealed a share to it.

To the holder who started it: what their client needs to finish the recovery: the session, the recovery key's record and maker's public halves, their own sealed share (held), the delivered shares (each with its holder's row and public halves), the vault's member-list chain (entries), the recovery member's wrap of the current key version (recoveryWrap), and the vault's revision.

The holder who started a recovery ends it, in one transaction that names the vault revision it was made from (expectedRevision): the next member list (entry), signed by the recovery key as the vault's recovery member, giving the session's member their new key and changing nothing else; the vault key wrapped to that key (wrap); and, when the member was a manager, a new wrap for each member whose wrap their old key signed (rewraps). Needs k − 1 other holders' shares in the session (from holders who still hold VAULT_RECOVERY), the new key still the member's active one, VAULT_RECOVERY and a recent sign-in. The member's wraps to the lost key are deleted. The recovery key is then marked used (usedDate): the recovering client held it whole, so the managers of every vault that lists it are told to replace it (remove#VaultMember of it, listing the new recovery key in the same rotation). An event and a notice to every member of the vault.
The holder who started a recovery, the member it recovers, or any other person in the vault's member list (each is told of the start) cancels it before it completes. An event.
A vault's events, newest first, to a member of it; with no vaultId, the events the caller made or that were about them.
